body.statement: At \(P^\star\), the displayed selected functions solve \(T_ah_a^{\mathrm{sel}}=g_a\) and \(T_a^*q_a^{\mathrm{sel}}=1\), and the positive finite law satisfies the bounded-moment, adjoint-range, stable-selection, and product-rate hypotheses used by ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023Nonuniqueness Theorem \(3.4\) and Corollary \(B.1\), as well as the selected-limit conditions of BennettEtAl2026StronglyIdentified Theorems \(3\), \(6\), and \(7\). Thus the Zhang estimator is root-\(n\), regular, asymptotically linear, and locally semiparametrically efficient on its additional-regularity model, and the Bennett construction is regular and asymptotically linear for the selected pair. On the joint positive rank-two chart, however, their selected-pair score obeys \[V_{\mathrm{sel}}=4432/1875=V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P^\star)+9496288/200416125>V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P^\star).\] Smooth bridge continuation and continuity of the normal Gram matrix preserve this strict gap on a relatively open neighborhood.
body.justification: The exact inequality respects Zhang et al.'s existing local efficiency result while isolating the new comparison: global efficiency across bridge pairs in the smaller simultaneous-existence observed-law model.
body.gap: ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023Nonuniqueness already proves root-\(n\), regular, asymptotically linear estimation and local semiparametric efficiency under additional regularity, and BennettEtAl2026StronglyIdentified proves regular selected-pair inference; neither computes the strictly smaller joint-model affine quotient variance on this assumption-matched positive chart.
body.consumer: The SUPPORT workflow gains a certificate for when a valid locally efficient selected-bridge standard error is not variance-minimizing in the joint observed-law experiment.
